# Support Escalation Policy (3-Tier Model)

## Purpose
This policy defines the structure, responsibilities, and escalation criteria for technical support across three tiers. It ensures timely resolution, clear ownership, and consistent customer experience while optimizing resource utilization.

---

## Tier 1: First Line / Frontline Support
**Role:** Initial point of contact; triage, diagnosis, and resolution of standard issues.

| **Scope** | • Answering inbound inquiries (phone, chat, email)  
• Resetting passwords, account access, basic configuration  
• Guiding customers through knowledge-base articles & FAQs  
• Creating/updating tickets in the tracking system  
• Basic troubleshooting using standardized scripts |
|---|---|
| **Typical Issues Handled** | Account questions, billing queries, "how-to" guidance, known issues with workarounds, minor UI glitches |
| **Escalation Triggers to Tier 2** | ❗ Issue not resolved within **4 business hours** of ticket creation  
❓ Problem requires access beyond agent permissions (API keys, admin panels, logs)  
❗ Customer reports critical impact (business disruption, data loss, compliance risk)  
❓ Request involves third-party integration, custom setup, or non-standard configuration  
❗ Customer explicitly requests Tier 2+ or has prior SLA-tier entitlement |
| **Handoff Requirements** | Ticket summary, customer context, steps already taken, screenshots/logs, urgency flag |

---

## Tier 2: Technical / Advanced Support
**Role:** Deep-dive troubleshooting; bridge between customers and engineering/product teams.

| **Scope** | • Detailed root-cause analysis using logs, metrics, and diagnostic tools  
• Reproducing issues in staging/dev environments when possible  
• Coordinating with product management or dev leads for config/code changes  
• Providing temporary mitigations or patches  
• Managing escalated tickets through resolution or hand-off to Tier 3 |
|---|---|
| **Typical Issues Handled** | Complex bugs, performance degradation, integration failures, recurring T1-escalated issues, configuration errors, security-hardening questions |
| **Escalation Triggers to Tier 3** | ❗ Root cause not identified within **24 business hours** of Tier 2 assumption  
❓ Issue requires a code change, schema migration, or architectural modification  
❗ Confirmed product bug with no existing workaround  
❓ Customer is on Enterprise/Gold-tier SLA with binding uptime/commitments  
❗ Security, privacy, or compliance violation suspected  
❓ Multiple independent tickets converge on the same underlying defect |
| **Handoff Requirements** | Full diagnostic dump, reproduction steps, environment details, customer impact assessment, tentative timeline, all prior correspondence |

---

## Tier 3: Expert / Engineering / Product Group
**Role:** Root-cause resolution; product-level fixes; strategic alignment.

| **Scope** | • Ownership of confirmed product defects end-to-end  
• Collaboration with R&D, QA, and architecture teams for permanent fixes  
• Release of patches, hotfixes, or version updates  
• Post-mortem analysis and knowledge-base enrichment  
• Approval for workarounds that affect multiple customers or systems |
|---|---|
| **Typical Issues Handled** | Core platform bugs, outage-causing failures, scalability limits, security vulnerabilities, API contract changes, major feature enhancements |
| **Escalation Triggers (Termination)** | ❗ Fix deployed and validated  
❓ Post-mortem completed; preventive measures implemented  
❗ Customer issue resolved or viable long-term workaround confirmed  
❓ SLA commitment met or formally amended via contract amendment |
| **Handoff Requirements** | Root cause analysis, fix description/change list, testing results, deployment plan, updated KB articles, communication template for affected customers |

---

## Escalation Matrix (Tiers → Next Tier)

| **From → To** | **Primary Trigger** | **Secondary Triggers** | **Max Time Before Escalation** |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 → T2 | Issue beyond agent scope / 4h no resolution | Critical impact, customer request, third-party involvement | 4 business hours |
| T2 → T3 | Root cause unidentified / 24h elapsed | Confirmed product bug, Enterprise SLA breach, security/compliance flag | 24 business hours |
| T3 → Resolution | Fix delivered / Post-mortem complete | Customer accepted workaround / SLA fulfilled | As per release timeline (typically < 5 business days) |

---

## Handoff Protocol
1. **Ticket Tagging:** Add `escalated-to-T2` or `escalated-to-T3` tag + timestamp.
2. **Summary Note:** Paste prior activity, customer quotes, and current status in the ticket description.
3. **Notify Stakeholders:** Auto-email to next-tier group + account manager (if applicable).
4. **SLA Clock:** Escalation resets or pauses SLA clock per company policy (commonly: "escalated tickets pause customer-facing SLA, internal SLA restarts upon resolution").
5. **Close Loop:** On resolution, update ticket status, log outcome in KB, and notify the customer with clarity on what was done.

---

## Review & Maintenance
- **Quarterly review** of escalation volumes, average time-in-tier, and recurring trigger patterns.
- Update tier scopes and time thresholds annually or when product/feature roadmap shifts significantly.
- Maintain a living **Escalation Playbook** referencing common scenarios, runbooks, and contact matrices.

---
*This policy applies to all customer-facing technical support channels. Exceptions require approval from the Support Manager or Director of Customer Success.*
